label: copy-phase input digit 1, late in long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost exclusively (98% of mass) when the fed-back input token is the digit 1 (a few weak activations on fed-back 0). Never fires in the original phase or on <DEL>, and essentially never when the 1 is one of the first two recalled tokens (recall_idx <= 2). Rate and mass grow with sequence length (L=9 holds 58% of mass, L<=5 almost none) and absolute step (t >= 12 holds ~80% of mass); also more likely when the sequence contains several digits. Top activations are a fed-back 1 at original position 3-5 of an L=8-9 sequence, often followed by another digit. Precision is low (~25%): most copy-phase 1 inputs in long sequences do not activate, and the deciding factor was not found with simple token/position variables.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: 1, 0, j, f, z, -; least: b, e, q, l) and the token being output (most: 0, 1, j, f, z, y; least: v, -, l, k); timing cues that raise it most: t=13, L=9 & t=13, t=12.
